result.headline: Layer 6 plugs into a Link trait built exactly to spec, but foreign messages have no home anywhere: store, contract, SSE and UI are all keyed by 32 B NodeIds. The fabric's routing is connection-oriented and plans fragments at queue time. The daemon wires one link, one Meshtastic binding, a read-only snapshot sidecar, and rnsd with share_instance = no.
findings: Link trait as built = L5 §8 (50-messaging/crates/mesh111/src/link/mod.rs:255-276) plus side seams LinkEvent :280, AnnounceGate :308, Dialer :324. A second driver registers via Fabric::add_link (mesh111/src/fabric.rs:740, :1377). There is no remove_link, and connections are keyed by slot index (fabric.rs:1004).

The fabric sends only to an attributed (link, PeerAddr) connection. route() is Direct/Hub/None (fabric.rs:1600-1620). sendable_conn takes the first attributed connection in BTreeMap order and ignores cost_class (fabric.rs:1570-1581). PeerAddr::Broadcast is never used. A radio driver must present each heard 111 peer as PeerAddr::Opaque plus LinkEvent::Connected and emit its own announce, as tcp-lan does (link/tcp_lan.rs:10-18).

No transit relay of sealed 111 traffic is built. Dir::Transit is a schema value only (mesh111/src/store/rows.rs:127). Cross-link carriage exists only as member-to-home-hub custody (pump_hub, fabric.rs:1961).

The fragment plan is fixed at queue time from the route MTU, else the smallest registered link MTU (fabric.rs:1631-1651). seal_data returns None when a fragment exceeds the link's room (fabric.rs:1808-1810), and pump_direct skips it silently (fabric.rs:1939-1941). Registering a 160 B link replans every no-route send, and long texts then fail TooLarge (fabric.rs:2922-2923).

The L6 shim byte is length-only: SHIM_LEN (mesh111/src/envelope.rs:60), payload_budget (:1346), shim_len (link/mod.rs:109). No frame_type/hop_limit codec exists, every Frame has hop_limit None (link/mod.rs:158-176), and FrameType::Foreign is dropped on receive (fabric.rs:2167).

INTRO is accepted only on tcp-lan (fabric.rs:2331-2341). Link::send is awaited inside the actor (fabric.rs:1203), so radio drivers must enqueue and return at once, as tcp-lan's try_send does (tcp_lan.rs:620-626).

Foreign messages cannot use the store or the contract as built: messages.peer/sender CHECK(length=32) (mesh111/src/store/schema.rs:71-72), SCHEMA_VERSION 2 (:43); Message/Thread/SseMessage.peer are NodeIds (40-interface/api/openapi.yaml:695-731, 938-944); routes need 64 hex (10-bootstrap/crates/node111/src/daemon/fabric/json.rs:50); the UI route /messages/:peer takes a NodeId only (40-interface/ui/src/views/messages/model.ts:194; app/routes.tsx:39-41).

The daemon wires one link: Live{tcp: Option<TcpLan>} (node111/src/daemon/fabric/mod.rs:170-174), construction :481-505, shutdown stops tcp only (:992-994). It reads one Meshtastic binding (node111/src/daemon/devices/store.rs:13-15; meshtastic/mod.rs:559).

Daemon-sidecar today is a one-way snapshot file, polled every 2 s (node111/src/daemon/meshtastic/presence.rs:1-25). A test forbids the presence sidecar any send path (50-messaging/sidecars/meshtastic-presence/tests/test_presence.py:582). Children get stdin null (node111/src/daemon/supervise.rs:333). The only credentialed precedent is the agent's env token plus loopback API (node111/src/daemon/intelligence.rs:44, :233), and that bearer is refused on writes (dashboard/api_v1/messages.rs:26-28).

The meshmud downlink 127.0.0.1:11230 is multi-client by design, and the L5 spec names a later meshtastic-client (50-messaging/README.md:603-606). The shim reframes 0x94C3 frames without decoding (meshtastic/shim.rs:1-10). Its 'no GPL in this binary' line and the module's 'never transmits' line (meshtastic/mod.rs:6-7) predate D22/D23.

rnsd: share_instance = no (10-bootstrap/crates/node111/assets/rns/config.tmpl:9), so no LXMF app can attach. The renderer is a constant template with SCHEMA_VERSION 1 and a takeover check (transport/config.rs:9-57). Restarts use pkill -f outside the supervisor (transport/mod.rs:178). rnsd ports are not in the PortTable; ownership is inferred from config stanzas (devices/registry.rs:1460-1466).

Identify lives in the Meshtastic module and is gated on meshmud plus the reader being installed (meshtastic/identify.rs:200-202). It claims the port and the downlink (meshtastic/mod.rs:668-675). Exit 3 persists family unknown, meaning only 'not Meshtastic' (identify.rs:24-26). PortTable claim/release/transfer is reusable (node111/src/daemon/ports.rs:106-190).

Panels: kind child/detected (reverse proxy, WebSocket) is refused (node111/src/daemon/panels/manifest.rs:398-405), and a panel id must be a ServiceId (manifest.rs:10). ServiceId is fixed at 9 (services/mod.rs:80-108), so a MeshChatX/LXMF panel needs both.

L2 TransportId has only nostr 0x01 (20-identity/crates/id111/src/attest.rs:150-170), so the A10 bridge identities (50-messaging/README.md:781) are unbuilt. Agent tools are pinned at 10 by tests (30-intelligence/crates/agent111/tests/daemon_tools.rs:306, chat_loop.rs:308). Daemon access from tools is GET-only (agent111/src/tools.rs:419). Proposal KINDS is fixed at 5 (dashboard/api_v1/proposals.rs:65; openapi.yaml:556).

Test counts on 2026-10-19: mesh111 161 (lib 136, 7 integration binaries 23, doctests 2) · node111 472 (lib 274, 22 integration binaries 198) · agent111 115 · id111 236 · UI vitest 1153 in 35 files · presence sidecar 69 (9 skipped).
result.recommendation: Foreign store: (A) additive schema-V3 tables plus typed Fabric calls in the mesh111 SQLCipher store, giving one key, one prune and one local_seq, but it amends locked L5 §10.3. (B) A separate bridge store in node111, which costs a second key and prune. (C) Pseudo-NodeIds in messages: reject. Pick A, if the owner allows the amendment. Bridge channel: (A) a spool dir, one file per message, reusing the presence hardening. (B) A loopback socket with a per-spawn token. (C) An in-binary Rust Meshtastic client on the meshmud downlink (D22 allows GPL). Pick C for Meshtastic and A for LXMF and phone apps. Sealed carriage needs Opaque per-peer connections, a shim codec, the fragment-plan fix and a cost-aware route.
open_questions: May Layer 6 amend the locked L5 store and fabric (schema V3 and a Class for foreign rows, cost-aware routing, re-planning unsent fragments, a shim codec, remove_link)? Or must the bridge live entirely outside mesh111?
Does 'a node on several networks relays between them' include sealed 111 traffic (new transit forwarding; Dir::Transit is unbuilt), or only readable text in each network's native format?
Meshtastic bridge: an in-binary Rust client (D22 permits GPL-3.0 linking) or a separate GPL sidecar beside the read-only presence reader?
LXMF needs share_instance = yes (assets/rns/config.tmpl:9) plus a separate LXMF process, and its hosted UI needs the deferred child-panel proxy and a new ServiceId. Are both in Layer 6 scope?
A10: which TransportId values and binding form for Meshtastic (the board holds an X25519 key, no signing key) and Reticulum (64 B key, hash binding)? This is an L2 registry amendment.

result.lens: LENS 3 - Phone apps via Termux (parked P2): what is honestly feasible
result.headline: Promise in v1 a small app-peer adapter with two hub-side reference adapters (SimpleX, Delta Chat); Briar is online-only (Tor), and ADB/UI driving of a phone stays a user-attended KB experiment outside the v1 promise.

candidates.name: SimpleX Chat CLI + smp-server
candidates.why: Documented bot WebSocket API (simplex-chat -p 5225, peerType bot) and LAN server via 'smp-server init --ip'. CLI v7.0.3 (2026-09-26), simplexmq v7.1.0-beta.4 (2026-10-17). Ubuntu glibc binaries only, no Android CLI; AGPL so separate process only.

candidates.name: Delta Chat: deltachat-rpc-server + chatmail relay
candidates.why: JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, Config::Bot flag, release v2.63.0 (2026-10-09) ships linux x86_64/aarch64 AND android arm64-v8a binaries so a Termux phone can be a node. LAN needs a chatmail relay (Debian 12 mail stack; IP-only mode explicitly experimental, self-signed TLS).

candidates.name: briar-headless
candidates.why: REST + WebSocket API works (contacts, private messages, tick events) but HeadlessModule.kt:99-104 registers only the Tor plugin on Linux, so it is gateway-class (internet on both sides); contacts are added over Tor hidden services. Briar 1.5.22 (2026-10-09). JVM jar.

candidates.name: Briar Desktop
candidates.why: DesktopModule.kt registers Tor + LAN + Mailbox on Linux, so the offline LAN transport exists, but it is a Compose GUI with no API. 0.6.5-beta.

candidates.name: Jami (jami-daemon + OpenDHT)
candidates.why: D-Bus API has sendMessage/getConversations and docs.jami.net/user/lan-only.html describes LAN with a bootstrap node, but offline failures are reported and the C++ daemon is heavy; no Termux build known.

candidates.name: Berty / Wesh Protocol
candidates.why: 'berty daemon' gRPC exists, but README says protocol only partially implemented and API unstable; last release v2.471.14 (2026-07-03); BLE discovery only in the mobile app.

candidates.name: Bitchat (iOS + Android)
candidates.license: Unlicense (iOS); Android LICENSE.md is GPL-3.0 though README says public domain
candidates.why: BLE mesh with no API or headless peer; joining from a hub means writing a BlueZ implementation (reinvention); Termux has no BLE.

candidates.name: Matrix: Tuwunel + matrix-rust-sdk
candidates.why: Note only (out of lens). Tuwunel v1.9.4 (2026-10-10), SDK 0.19.1 (2026-09-18); the only candidate that could link in-binary in Rust after D22; matterbridge is stale (pushed 2024-12).

candidates.name: Termux + Termux:API
candidates.why: Already bundled in L1 (10-bootstrap/README.md:40). Offers notifications (incl. termux-notification-list), SMS, clipboard, share, SAF, termux-open; no UI driving, silent install, or Bluetooth. App stable tag v0.118.3 (2025-05-22), api-package v0.60.0 (2026-09-16).

candidates.name: adb (android-tools) inside Termux, wireless debugging to the same phone
candidates.why: Works Android 11+ with a Wi-Fi association and one-time human pairing, but the connection port changes per session and it drops on screen lock/reboot/network change (Android 17 ADB Wi-Fi 2.0 auto-offs on untrusted networks): attended experiment only.

candidates.name: Meshtastic / MeshCore Android apps
candidates.why: No stable app API; board path (lens 1) is the real one. Meshtastic google flavor on Android 16+ exposes an AppFunctions sendMessage, callable only with EXECUTE_APP_FUNCTIONS or via 'adb shell cmd app_function' (preview) - experiment only.

candidates.name: Session
candidates.why: Onion-routed over its own service-node network; no LAN or offline mode found (unverified, secondary source).

findings: briar-headless registers ONLY the Tor plugin on Linux (HeadlessModule.kt:99-104, https://github.com/briar/briar/blob/master/briar-headless/src/main/java/org/briarproject/briar/headless/HeadlessModule.kt), so Briar cannot be an offline-LAN bridge target from a hub; the offline transports exist only in the Android app (no API) and Briar Desktop (GUI, DesktopModule.kt:71-75). A hub is a Briar contact of the phone user only over Tor with internet on both sides; nearby add is app-only (headless README L257).

deltachat-rpc-server v2.63.0 (2026-10-09) ships android arm64-v8a plus linux aarch64/x86_64 binaries (https://github.com/chatmail/core/releases/tag/v2.63.0): the only candidate where a Termux phone can itself be a node. SimpleX CLI assets are Ubuntu/macOS/Windows only (https://github.com/simplex-chat/simplex-chat/releases/tag/v7.0.3).

SimpleX documents bot participation (bots/README.md, WebSocket -p 5225) and a LAN server form 'smp-server init -y -l --ip 192.168.1.5' (docs/SERVER.md L606-633): the strongest offline-LAN fit. chatmail LAN needs a Debian 12 Postfix/Dovecot stack and IP-only mode is 'experimental and might change without notice' (https://github.com/chatmail/relay/blob/main/doc/source/iponly.rst).

agent111 is 'no shell, no plugins, ever' (30-intelligence/crates/agent111/src/tools.rs:1) and messages.send only writes a proposal (tools.rs:13-15): the lens premise 'the agent can run commands in Termux' does not hold today; ADB/termux-api actions must be typed 111d actions with human approval (parked P4), not agent tools.

Same-phone ADB is not a standing channel: needs Android 11+ and a Wi-Fi association, one-time human pairing, connection port changes per session, drops on screen lock/reboot (third-party notes, https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ferrumclaudepilgrim/claude-code-android@main/docs/adb-wireless.md); Android 17 'ADB Wi-Fi 2.0' auto-disables on untrusted networks (https://android-developers.googleblog.com/2026/09/wireless-debugging-adb-wifi-2.html). L1 already does host-over-USB adb provisioning (10-bootstrap/README.md:64-68).

APK install from Termux always needs a human tap: termux-open is ACTION_VIEW (https://github.com/termux/termux-tools/blob/master/scripts/termux-open.in); silent install is only 'pm install' via ADB (https://developer.android.com/tools/adb). Android developer verification starts 2026-09-30 for participating stores in BR/ID/SG/TH, global in 2027, and Google says the adb workflow 'stays the same' (https://developer.android.com/developer-verification/guides).

Reading another app's data is impossible by design (https://source.android.com/docs/security/app-sandbox); the only read paths are app exports and notifications (termux-notification-list), and Android 13+ restricted settings may block the Notification Access grant for sideloaded Termux:API (secondary sources).

Meshtastic-Android (google flavor, Android 16+) registers an AppFunctions sendMessage (androidApp/src/google/.../BaseMeshtasticAppFunctionService.kt) but callers need EXECUTE_APP_FUNCTIONS and Google calls the API an experimental preview (https://developer.android.com/ai/appfunctions); the board/meshmud path (lens 1) remains the real Meshtastic path.

KB corrections needed: 00-knowledge/projects/briar-bramble.md says GPL-3.0-only but Briar LICENSE.txt grants 'version 3 ... or any later version'; bitchat-android README says public domain but its LICENSE.md is GPL-3.0. Existing briar-mailbox.md claim 'headless registers only Tor on Linux' is confirmed.

Bridging makes the hub an endpoint holding the plaintext of an end-to-end-encrypted app, and forwarding it to LoRa publishes it: per-contact opt-in, honest labelling, and the D23 loop guard are mandatory; SimpleX and Delta Chat both have a bot flag to label the bridge account honestly.

License gate after D22: SimpleX (AGPL-3.0), Briar (GPL), Jami (GPL) should stay separate supervised processes; Delta Chat core (MPL-2.0), Berty (Apache/MIT), matrix-rust-sdk (Apache-2.0) could link in-binary but the sidecar pattern is cheaper. No Reticulum code is involved in any candidate.
result.recommendation: Fork A (v1 promise under 'phone apps'): (1) PICK: one app-peer adapter shape with two hub-side reference adapters, SimpleX (offline-LAN best) then Delta Chat (Termux node); (2) Briar-first, online-only; (3) Delta Chat only; (4) framework only. Fork B (ADB/UI driving): PICK not in v1, a runbook plus KB entry for a user-attended wizard where the agent only proposes typed actions that 111d executes after approval (narrow P4 cut); alternatives are an opt-in phone assistant in v1 or agent-owned shell (rejected, breaks 'no shell'). Fork C (Briar offline): do not carry a one-line LAN-plugin patch; document Briar as online-only gateway-class. If time is short: SimpleX adapter, Delta Chat adapter, Briar last. Tiers: (i) SimpleX, Delta Chat (Briar online-only); (ii) offline Briar, Bitchat, Meshtastic/MeshCore apps by ADB/UI; (iii) Session, centralized messengers, reading app data.
open_questions: Are SimpleX and Delta Chat acceptable as the two named v1 'phone apps', with Briar online-only because it has no offline headless path?
May the hub terminate an app's end-to-end encryption to bridge it (plaintext on the hub, per-contact opt-in, labelled in Messages and on foreign radios)?
The agent has no shell by design: approve moving adb/termux-api phone actions into human-approved typed 111d actions (a narrow cut of parked P4) in Layer 6?
Is a Debian/Ubuntu-class glibc hub an acceptable floor for the SimpleX and chatmail adapters, excluding musl-only boards from this category?
When the hub has internet, may it use public servers (chatmail relays, SimpleX preset servers) or self-hosted ones only?
Want a follow-up scout on Matrix (Tuwunel + matrix-rust-sdk, linkable in Rust after D22) and XMPP/Prosody, which were outside this lens?

result.lens: LENS 4 — BRIDGE DESIGN: categories, fan-out, relay between networks, loop guard, consent, prior art
result.headline: Build the bridge core in 111d: foreign messages go in their own V3 tables in the SQLCipher store, fan-out is per-target in one send group, relays are explicit directed edges with a marker-based loop guard. Prior art shows no usable core and no solved loop guard.

candidates.name: matterbridge (original)
candidates.why: Star gateway, RemoteNickFormat prefix template and a REST API gateway. No Meshtastic or LXMF backend. Loop safety is topological (never send back to the same channel+account). Clips at 400 characters by default and its ID map is an in-memory LRU. Last push 2024-12-12. Verified via GitHub metadata and README, not the LICENSE file.

candidates.name: matterbridge-org fork
candidates.why: Active (last push 2026-10-09), needs Go 1.26, no Meshtastic or LXMF protocol. Not the core: persistence, consent, byte limits and per-target state would all be ours anyway. Possible later Layer 7 internet-chat gateway as a separate process.

candidates.name: mmrelay (meshtastic-matrix-relay)
candidates.why: Per PyPI and the repo page, LICENSE file not read. Release 1.4.1 on 2026-10-14. Default prefix {display5}[M]: leaves about 200 characters. message_delay floor 2.0 s. Loop guard and DM handling undocumented. Prefix pattern only.

candidates.name: MTMC Bridge
candidates.why: Rust, beta, updated 2026-08-08. Star relay Meshtastic to MeshCore public channels with a [name] message prefix and an unspecified one-line anti-recirculation rule. License from the project page only.

candidates.name: Meshenger
candidates.license: MIT (README); GitHub license field is null
candidates.why: Rust TCP client on a Meshtastic node bridging to Telegram and Discord with a [TG:alice] prefix, per-module public/DM/both scope, queue with pacing and jitter. Shape reference for the in-binary Meshtastic adapter.

candidates.name: LXMF-Tools lxmf_bridge_meshtastic
candidates.why: Verified via GitHub metadata. The only Meshtastic to LXMF text bridge from a known author. Beta, last push 2025-03-19, README is a stub. Python on the RNS/LXMF stack (source not read, unverified), so pattern-only under rule 1.

candidates.name: Splice (Meshtastic channel to LXMF group)
candidates.why: Known only from a search summary because the page returned 404. MQTT in, gateway HTTP out, member list in config, bridge holds no channel key. Recent commits May 2026 (unverified). Design idea only.

candidates.name: matrix-lxmf (Matrix to LXMF puppeting bridge)
candidates.why: README states no license has been chosen. Portal-room-per-contact plus ghost user is the useful pattern. Requires a shared rnsd instance and imports RNS.

candidates.name: mautrix bridges (relay mode, portal/ghost model)
candidates.why: LICENSE file read. Relay mode is opt-in per room, admin-only by default, with a sender-name prefix. Matrix is the hub, so the design is not adoptable. Pattern only.

candidates.name: biboumi (XMPP to IRC gateway)
candidates.why: License from the page statement, COPYING file not read. Last commit 2026-10-11. Design principle: partial mapping by design, enforce the target network's rules and tell the user.

findings: No chat-bridge core has a Meshtastic or LXMF backend: the 42wim README lists 19 protocols without either (https://github.com/42wim/matterbridge) and the fork's docs/protocols has none (https://github.com/matterbridge-org/matterbridge/tree/master/docs/protocols). Its REST API (POST /api/message, GET /api/stream, bearer token) is the only extension point (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/42wim/matterbridge/API.md).

Matterbridge's loop safety is topological: SendMessage skips the originating channel+account, there is no own-user check, and the ID map is an in-memory LRU(5000) (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/42wim/matterbridge/master/gateway/gateway.go). It clips at MessageLength 400 characters by default and drops overflow from a 30-message queue (https://github.com/42wim/matterbridge/wiki/Settings), the opposite of delivery-first.

Every Meshtastic relay found attributes with an in-text prefix: mmrelay {display5}[M]: (about 200 characters left), MTMC [name] message, Meshenger [TG:alice]. None documents a loop guard beyond MTMC's one sentence, so the loop guard is ours (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeremiah-k/meshtastic-matrix-relay/main/docs/ADVANCED_CONFIGURATION.md, https://sourceforge.net/p/mtmc-bridge/).

Size facts: Data.payload max 233 B (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/meshtastic/protobufs/master/meshtastic/mesh.options); the Android composer caps at 200 B as a UI choice (https://meshtastic.org/docs/software/android/user/messages-and-channels/); about 221 B with PKI (00-knowledge/projects/meshtastic.md:64). LXMF opportunistic content is at most 287 B, link packet 319 B, larger as a resource (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/markqvist/LXMF/master/LXMF/LXMessage.py).

Meshtastic exposes flow-control and refusal facts: QueueStatus{res,free,maxlen,mesh_packet_id}, Routing.Error TOO_LARGE=7, DUTY_CYCLE_LIMIT=9, RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED=38 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/meshtastic/protobufs/master/meshtastic/mesh.proto). The node transmits nothing with no region set and stops at the duty-cap (EU_868 10%, EU_866 2.5%) unless overridden (https://meshtastic.org/docs/configuration/radio/lora/).

Meshtastic delivery evidence: broadcasts get only an implicit ACK from a heard rebroadcast (up to 3 sends); DMs get a real recipient ACK (up to 5 sends). A channel broadcast can never honestly reach delivered (https://meshtastic.org/docs/overview/mesh-algo/). LXMF: a propagated send stops at SENT; DELIVERED needs recipient confirmation (LXMessage.py above).

LXMF fields FIELD_CUSTOM_TYPE/DATA/META (0xFB-0xFD), FIELD_REPLY_TO 0x30, FIELD_REACTION 0x40 and FIELD_GROUP 0x0B exist (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/markqvist/LXMF/master/LXMF/LXMF.py), so the relay/loop marker costs no visible bytes on the LXMF side. Meshtastic has only the in-text marker.

Meshtastic channel identity is name+PSK, not the local-only index (MeshPacket.channel comment in mesh.proto; https://meshtastic.org/docs/configuration/radio/channels/). Channel-message senders are unauthenticated: PSK channels are encrypted but not authenticated (00-knowledge/projects/meshtastic-pki.md:25-28). Data has native reply_id/emoji and a bitfield whose first use is the MQTT-upload approval; the bit position is unverified.

Meshtastic's own off-mesh consent convention is ok_to_mqtt (default-key channels only, 'a polite request that is enforced in the official firmware') plus Ignore MQTT (https://meshtastic.org/docs/configuration/radio/lora/). Community bot norms (regional, not official): reply by DM, avoid the default public channel, put 'bot' in the node name, do not answer bots (https://areyoumeshingwith.us/docs/general/bots-and-automation/).

mautrix relay mode is opt-in per room, admin-only by default, name-prefixed, and does not bridge reactions from relayed users (https://docs.mau.fi/bridges/general/relay-mode.html). Matrix's m.notice convention is a structural 'bots ignore this' marker (spec mirror, wording unverified). biboumi maps partially on purpose and tells users the target's rules (https://codeberg.org/poezio/biboumi).

Meshtastic to LXMF text bridges exist (LXMF-Tools lxmf_bridge_meshtastic, MIT, last push 2025-03-19; Splice, May 2026) but are Python on the RNS/LXMF stack, so pattern-only under hard rule 1. matrix-lxmf has no license and is rejected.

Store: messages.peer/sender are CHECK(length=32) (50-messaging/crates/mesh111/src/store/schema.rs:71-72) and the schema is migrated append-only from SCHEMA_VERSION=2 (schema.rs:43), so foreign messages need V3 tables, never pseudo-NodeIds. L5 section 14 and N/meshtastic/mod.rs:6-7 still say 111 never transmits; D23 supersedes. Proposal.kind is a closed enum (40-interface/api/openapi.yaml:556). A10 lets a 111 node recognise another 111 bridge, but TransportId has only nostr 0x01 (20-identity/crates/id111/src/attest.rs:150-170, via lens 0).
result.recommendation: Fork picks. Store: A, additive V3 tables (foreign conversations, messages, relay edges, send groups) in the SQLCipher store with a Class::Foreign prune slot (alternatives: separate node111 store, memory-only, pseudo-NodeIds). Categories: per-network rail with channels and DMs, never merged with 111 threads; 'Message them' opens a native radio DM, never a contact. Fan-out: one send group, one message per target, preview, refuse by default, explicit split, never silent truncation. Relay: explicit directed non-transitive edges, visible [name/TAG] marker (a structured field on LXMF), id map, own-echo suppression, never re-relay; DMs unrepresentable; human-only enable, agent proposes. Core: 111d (Rust) with in-binary Meshtastic adapter and sidecar adapters; matterbridge only later as an optional Layer 7 gateway. States carry an evidence string; broadcasts never reach delivered.
open_questions: May Layer 6 add V3 foreign tables, Class::Foreign and typed Fabric::foreign_* calls to the locked L5 store (same as lens 0 Q1)?
Post a 'this channel is bridged by node N' notice on the source channel when an edge is enabled? It costs airtime; default on or off?
Honour Meshtastic ok_to_mqtt (the sender's opt-out from leaving the mesh) as a default relay filter on public default-key channels?
Is a visible [name/TAG] marker costing 8-14 B per relayed Meshtastic message acceptable?
Two 111 nodes relaying the same pair: warn only in v1 (pick) or build sealed relay-claim coordination?
Relay backlog: hold to capacity then shed oldest with a visible counter (pick), or hold everything?
Relay into an amateur-licensed radio: allow after human confirmation (pick) or block?

result.lens: Lens 5: Transports and the device core, scoped without hardware
result.headline: Build Layer 6 bridge-first on a minimal transport spine (interfaces.toml, posture, live-attach applier), ship device core in the first signed release (R-B), and defer the MeshCore kiss-modem link to a second release; D19 c stands but needs CI-built images and a dev-range data type until a bench demo exists.

candidates.name: MeshCore firmware + KISS modem env
candidates.why: KISS modem exists with a documented protocol and envs for Heltec V3/V4, RAK4631, T-Beam, T3S3; repeaters flood GRP_DATA blind; but no kiss CI or release tag, so 111 must CI-build and pin images; data-type IDs are granted only after a working demo, so use FF00-FFFF until the bench.

candidates.name: Reticulum rnsd/rnstatus/rnodeconf

meshtasticd -s is a simulated-radio mode on TCP port 4403 (PortduinoGlue.cpp:317), usable as a hardware-less Meshtastic stub; no prebuilt native binary is in the GitHub release assets

No official Meshtastic policy for automated senders was found; community guidance says DM replies, avoid the default public channel and MQTT-uplinked channels; https://areyoumeshingwith.us/docs/general/bots-and-automation/

result.recommendation: Fork A (sequencing): A1 transport-first per devices.md; A2 bridge-first on a minimal spine (interfaces.toml + posture share_instance=yes + live-attach applier + transport.read, then bridge core with Meshtastic and LXMF adapters, then phone relay v1, then device core, kiss-modem last) - PICK, because the LXMF adapter is blocked on rnsd posture and every bridge test runs in netns today; A3 two parallel tracks. Fork B (first signed release): R-A bridge+spine+phone relay; R-B R-A plus device core (identify, RNode stanza proposals, uevent) - PICK, fall back to R-A if the test setup slips; R-C adds kiss-modem and the 111 modem image (make it the second release). Identify with own byte probes for family detection and keep rnodeconf for provisioning/flash. Phone side: Termux plus TCP-to-hub only; Columba optional; build no helper APK in v1. Keep Python rnsd as-is.

MeshCore data type: ship on the shared dev range FF00-FFFF until the bench, or hold the kiss-modem release until a number_allocations PR can merge after a working demo?
Does leviculum's lnsd ever count as 'Reticulum as-is' under D17 #12, or is Python rnsd the only allowed implementation?
May the signed manifest bundle a Columba APK (embeds Reticulum-licensed Python RNS) or only link to it, and is the -no-sentry variant mandatory?
Meshtastic pin policy: bridge-tested on stable 2.7.26 only, or also on the 2.8.1 pre-release?
Is 'per-channel opt-in, DM-preferred, never on the default or MQTT-uplinked channel' an acceptable default for automated Meshtastic sends?
Identify probes: own byte probes for family detection (pick) or rnodeconf --info everywhere?

result.lens: LENS 2 — the Reticulum/LXMF bridge: our node as an LXMF endpoint without importing RNS
result.headline: Run MeshChatX 4.10.7 headless beside rnsd (shared instance) as the LXMF endpoint behind a swappable carrier trait; it needs no rule change but ends upstream on 2027-01-01, so the owner should decide the sidecar-import contingency (Option C) before building.

candidates.name: Reticulum rnsd (RNS 1.5.7)
candidates.why: Already our connected service. PyPI 1.5.7 on 2026-10-05, pure wheel. GitHub is a lagging public mirror with no support, so pin from PyPI hashes.

candidates.why: Needed in the venv. lxmd gives an inbound-only hook (no signature-valid flag, no send, default rejects inbound resources above 1,000 B) and an optional propagation-node role. 1.2.1 (2026-10-13) adds airtime-aware retries.

findings: Versions: RNS 1.5.7 (2026-10-05), LXMF 1.2.1 (2026-10-13), NomadNet 1.4.4, MeshChatX 4.10.7 (2026-10-11), all pure py3-none-any wheels; KB projects/reticulum.md (RNS 1.3.5, LXMF 1.0.1) and projects/lxmf.md (1.2.0) are stale. https://pypi.org/pypi/rns/json , https://pypi.org/pypi/lxmf/json

Upstream GitHub is a lagging public mirror with 'no support' (LXMF MIRROR.md, commit 2025-12-27): mirror at LXMF 1.2.0 / RNS tag 1.5.5 while PyPI has 1.2.1 / 1.5.7, so locks must come from PyPI hashes. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/markqvist/LXMF/master/MIRROR.md
MeshChatX README 'Project status': development and releases end 2027-01-01, v5.0.0 last release, repo then archived. https://github.com/Quad4-Software/MeshChatX

Reticulum's own default is share_instance = Yes but our template sets no (10-bootstrap/crates/node111/assets/rns/config.tmpl:9); a client started on default config tries to become the shared instance and only falls back to client when the bind fails (RNS/Reticulum.py ~405-460). Clients in other config dirs derive a different rpc_key (Reticulum.py:362) unless both carry the same rpc_key. Shared socket is abstract AF_UNIX \0rns/<instance> (LocalInterface.py:68), per network namespace, or 127.0.0.1:37428/37429 in tcp mode.

rnstatus --attach/--detach/--reload exist since RNS 1.5.5 and interface management is on by default (Reticulum.py:260,553), while 111d kills rnsd on interface change (src/daemon/transport/mod.rs:170-186), which would drop LXMF client sessions.

lxmd on_inbound writes a msgpack container {state, lxmf_bytes, transport_encrypted, transport_encryption, method} with no signature_validated flag, though LXMRouter.lxmf_delivery delivers unverified messages (LXMRouter.py:1906-1987); lxmd defaults: stamp cost 12 announced but not enforced, delivery_transfer_max_accepted_size = 1 means 1,000 B (LXMRouter.py:2048). No send path, no display names. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/markqvist/LXMF/master/LXMF/Utilities/lxmd.py

MeshChatX API read from source: POST /api/v1/lxmf-messages/send takes only content, destination_hash and image/audio/file/telemetry/commands/app_extensions(field 16), no title or arbitrary fields; message JSON has no verify flag; CSRF token from GET /api/v1/auth/csrf; WS /ws pushes lxmf_message and announce events; plugins cannot hook messages. https://github.com/Quad4-Software/MeshChatX/blob/master/meshchatx/src/backend/http/routes/lxmf.py , docs/en/plugins.md

MeshChatX has 20 hard requirements (wasmtime, aioquic, miniaudio, bleak, lxst); miniaudio ships no Linux aarch64 wheel; its Termux guide needs rust and build-essential. https://pypi.org/pypi/reticulum-meshchatx/json , https://pypi.org/pypi/miniaudio/json

LXMF wire: dest16 + source16 + sig64 + msgpack [timestamp, title, content, fields(, stamp)] (code is title-first; README prose says content first); overhead 112 B; opportunistic content <= 287 B, link packet <= 319 B, above that a Resource; message id = SHA-256(dest+source+payload); timestamp is sender wall-clock. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/markqvist/LXMF/master/LXMF/LXMessage.py

Delivery: DELIVERED = recipient proof; propagated send stops at SENT; MAX_DELIVERY_ATTEMPTS 5, retry wait 10 s then FAILED, so the 111 outbox must resubmit (delivery first). Maps to the four KB states queued/sent/relayed/delivered. LXMRouter.py:32-36 and LXMessage.py:570-583.

LXMF 1.2.1 (diff of wheel vs 1.2.0 mirror) adds AIRTIME_AWARE_MTU_TIME, slow-path cache and holds queued messages to slow destinations: LXMF will hold what we hand it, so 'sent' must follow its callbacks. Wheel sha256 4bd95325b00e5fae81241e28f26a5ed22b38fea941e128d1c63a33c99e931440.

Stamp cost to a sender: expected 2^cost attempts, each hashing a 768,000 B workblock (3000 x 256 B), cost 12 about 3 GB hashed per message; propagation stamps 16 (min 13), peering 18; FIELD_TICKET grants 21 days stamp-free. LXStamper.py:12,49-78,178-200; LXMessage.py:49-53.

LXMF has no channels: FIELD_GROUP 0x0B has no published meaning; FIELD_CUSTOM_TYPE/DATA 0xFB-0xFD are reserved for bridging; channel-like patterns are distribution-group endpoints (LXMF-Tools) and the separate RRC protocol. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/markqvist/LXMF/master/LXMF/LXMF.py

RNS identity file is 64 raw bytes (32 X25519 private + 32 Ed25519 seed), public key 64 B; A10 binds it into the 32 B transport_key by SHA-256 and 111d can make transport_sig from the seed (20-identity/README.md:223-236,366). Let the child create the identity and 111d only read it.

Discovery: peers appear only by announce (about 200 B, estimate); announce cap 2 % per interface; our AutoInterface group_id 111.network (config.tmpl:15) differs from stock default 'reticulum' (AutoInterface.py:49), so stock LAN users do not hear us without a second group or a TCP/Backbone listener with IFAC.

Upstream's brandolinis.rst (lines 127-142,153,195,203) says the protocol is public domain and may be implemented by a human from docs, but machine-generated copies of source are derivative; an LLM-built Rust LXMF stack is the contested case, so reimplementation is not a safe v1 path. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/markqvist/Reticulum/master/docs/source/brandolinis.rst
Test hygiene: far-end LXMF peers in netns tests must be adopted programs (MeshChatX, LXMF-Tools echo), not our scripts importing LXMF, or the LICENSING.md:30 evidence line breaks.
result.recommendation: Pick Option A: MeshChatX 4.10.7 headless child on loopback, attached to rnsd's shared instance (share_instance = yes, shared rpc_key, empty-interface client dir, enable_transport = no), with a thin Rust carrier adapter over its REST and WebSocket, also serving as panel P7. Hold Option C (a separate-process sidecar importing RNS/LXMF) as the owner's contingency because MeshChatX ends 2027-01-01 and exposes no signature-valid flag; its license consequences are spelled out in the report. lxmd is only an optional propagation node. Reject own-Rust, Leviculum, LXMF-rs, LXMFy, NomadNet, rnsh. Decide C before building the carrier.
open_questions: Accept MeshChatX knowing it ends 2027-01-01, or lift D17 #12 now for a sidecar importing RNS and LXMF (Option C)?

With no LXMF channels, what is the 'send to Reticulum' target: a chosen peer address, a distribution-group hub, or an RRC room later; and does 'same message in several networks' mean per-network recipient lists?
May the node join the public 'reticulum' AutoInterface group and/or open a LAN BackboneInterface with IFAC for stock apps?
Should the hub run as an opt-in LXMF propagation node (storage 500 MB default, stamp costs)?
Display name and announce interval for the bridge identity under the 2 % announce cap?
Is a 'sender unverified' label acceptable in v1 (A and lxmd expose no signature-valid flag), or must verification be shown (forces C)?
LXMF signs wall-clock timestamps: what time source for nodes without an RTC?
Is relay labelling (foreign sender in a text prefix, source always our bridge identity) acceptable?

findings: Firmware rate-limits phone-originated text to one per 2 s with a RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED NAK, drops repeated packet ids silently (window of 20), and the state is per PhoneAPI instance, shared by every meshmud downlink (panel user plus bridge): firmware src/mesh/PhoneAPI.cpp:795-867 @ v2.7.26.54e0d8d; meshmud forwards verbatim (internal/common/uplink.go:227-248).

The board's API session lapses after 15 minutes without any ToRadio (serial and TCP): src/SerialConsole.cpp:27,119-121, src/mesh/api/ServerAPI.cpp:6,34. The presence reader deliberately strips the heartbeat (50-messaging/sidecars/meshtastic-presence/README.md 'No send path'), so Nearby can freeze silently when no panel is open: a latent Layer 5 defect the bridge must fix with a nonce-0 heartbeat. Rust crate comment cites the same limit (meshtastic/rust src/connections/handlers.rs:17-19).

Heartbeat nonce 1 makes the node broadcast NodeInfo on the mesh (a transmit): PhoneAPI.cpp handleToRadio heartbeat case (~216-232); web SDK reserves it (meshtastic/web packages/sdk/src/core/client/handshake.ts:47-52). 111 must send nonce 0 or 2+ only.

The firmware rewrites from=0 then sets our node number (MeshService.cpp:188-193; Router.cpp send()), so the bridge speaks as the board's node. User.long_name is now limited to 24 bytes (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/meshtastic/protobufs/master/meshtastic/mesh.proto, commit 9370b7a of 2026-10-18); Data.payload max_size 233 (mesh.options:24). Firmware checks encoded Data against 255-16, minus 12 for PKI (RadioInterface.h:20-22, Router.cpp:658): about 232 B plain / 220 B PKI by my arithmetic; official composer cap 200 B (https://meshtastic.org/docs/software/android/user/messages-and-channels/).

DMs are PKI-only: they need the recipient public key in the board's NodeDB, else PKI_SEND_FAIL_PUBLIC_KEY (Router.cpp:648-695); a non-PKI text DM to us is rejected as legacy (Router.cpp:499); licensed (HAM) nodes skip PKI. A received DM arrives with to==my_node_num, pki_encrypted=true, public_key set.

Ack mapping: a ROUTING_APP packet with request_id == our id and error NONE is an implicit ack when its from equals our own node number (relay overheard) and a real delivery ack otherwise (meshtastic-python node.py:1062-1068). Channel broadcasts have want_ack forced off on air (Router.cpp:333-336) but get 3 local retransmissions (NextHopRouter.h:93) ending in an implicit ack or MAX_RETRANSMIT NAK, so channel text can only reach 'relayed'. DUTY_CYCLE_LIMIT and RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED mean retry later.

meshmud multiplexing (clone fabe043): every FromRadio goes to every downlink (uplink.go:145-153) with drop-when-full; uplink loss closes all downlinks (dtcp/listener.go:123-139); mesh_packet_dedupe=true would reject a second client (dtcp/listener.go:78-82); no DTR/RTS handling. Any client's want_config_id restarts the config stream for all; the web client uses special nonces 69420/69421 and warns re-sending want_config 'can wedge firmware' (handshake.ts:1-21).

MQTT: our own packets are uplinked whenever the channel has uplink_enabled (ok_to_mqtt gates only others' packets, MQTT.cpp:782-786); PKI DMs are uplinked as opaque blobs when any channel has uplink (MQTT.cpp:772-775,796-798); via_mqtt/ignore_mqtt exist (Router.cpp:868). Public server is zero-hop with a portnum filter (https://meshtastic.org/docs/software/integrations/mqtt/). Bridge must show the channel's uplink state before the first send.

Inbound text is lost while no client reads: toPhoneQueue holds 8 or 32 packets and discards the oldest text (MeshService.cpp:319-335, mesh-pb-constants.h:16-21). The firmware does not echo phone-sent text to other clients (MeshService.cpp:208,247,263), so the web panel will not list bridge-sent messages (unverified on hardware).

result.headline: MeshChatX 4.10.7 passed every functional and egress check on the lead box and is viable as the LXMF carrier in a slim 35-wheel closure on a bundled CPython 3.11 with rnsd left on the distro Python, but it fails the device floor on Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 11 and Termux unless the owner accepts python-build-standalone or the Option C rule change.

candidates.name: MeshChatX 4.10.7, slim closure (35 wheels, run as a separate supervised process)
candidates.why: Run: attaches to rnsd shared instance, send/receive via REST+WS, field 16 round-trips, 0 egress in 10 min idle and whole session, rnsd restart reconnects in 7 s, 33 MB wheels, 128 MiB on disk, 75 MB RSS, 0.4 s warm start. Needs Python >=3.11. Upstream sunset 2027-01-01 (v5.0.0 last). Dropping lxst/numpy/miniaudio/pycodec2/wasmtime/bleak/dbus-fast/aioquic/pylsqpack is unsupported by upstream but worked for messaging.

candidates.name: MeshChatX 4.10.7, full closure (44 wheels)
candidates.why: Also works (run) but 251 MiB site-packages, 87.6 MB RSS, miniaudio has no aarch64 wheel (manylinux or musllinux) so Pi-class nodes need a source or CI build; lxst/numpy need Python >=3.11 anyway.

findings: PyPI reticulum-meshchatx 4.10.7 (2026-10-11): requires_python >=3.11, license 0BSD AND MIT, 21 direct requires_dist; pip resolves a 44-wheel closure of 67.3 MB; all hashes cross-checked with PyPI digests (https://pypi.org/pypi/reticulum-meshchatx/4.10.7/json). The 3.11 floor is real: tomllib, StrEnum and datetime.UTC are used (installed wheel, src/ tree).

Default python3: Debian 11 = 3.9.2-3, Debian 12 = 3.11.2-1, Debian 13 = 3.13.5-1 (https://sources.debian.org/api/src/python3-defaults/); Ubuntu 22.04 = 3.10.x, 24.04 = 3.12.3 (Launchpad getPublishedSources python3-defaults); Pi OS trixie is Debian 13 (https://www.raspberrypi.com/news/trixie-the-new-version-of-raspberry-pi-os/); Termux python 3.14.8 (https://packages.termux.dev/apt/termux-main/dists/stable/main/binary-aarch64/Packages).

Wheel matrix (cp311): every dependency has manylinux x86_64 and musllinux x86_64 wheels; manylinux aarch64 and musllinux aarch64 have everything except miniaudio 1.71 (sdist only). Termux has Android wheels only for aiohttp and wasmtime; Termux packages exist for cryptography 50.0.2, bcrypt, psutil, numpy; cborx, aioquic, cffi, pylsqpack, dbus-fast, miniaudio, pycodec2 would compile (whether Termux pip selects Android tags is unverified).

Run: MeshChatX attaches as a shared-instance client (rnstatus 'Serving: 1 program'; only rnsd owns @rns/nodeA and its /rpc). Run: if MeshChatX starts before rnsd it becomes the instance and a later rnsd attaches as a client with no TCP link, silently partitioning the node; start order must be rnsd first.

Run: --auth is a no-op in 4.10.7 (auth_enabled false, anonymous GET /api/v1/config returns 200). Auth needs POST /api/v1/auth/setup plus PATCH /api/v1/config {auth_enabled:true}; then 401 anonymous, 403 csrf_invalid without X-CSRF-Token, login rotates the token; WS /ws rejects foreign Origin (403) and missing cookie (401).

Run: incoming message arrives on B's WS as {type:'lxmf.delivery', remote_identity_name, lxmf_message:{hash, source_hash, destination_hash, is_incoming, state, method, title, content, fields, timestamp, rssi, snr, quality, ...}} (lens 2's 'lxmf_message' event name is the outgoing-created event). No signature-valid flag; src: SIGNATURE_INVALID is dropped (meshchat.py ~9955), SOURCE_UNKNOWN is delivered unflagged. Message hash is identical on both ends.

Run: fields.app_extensions (LXMF field 16) set on send arrives byte-identical in the WS and REST JSON, including nested objects. Src: send path ignores unknown field ids and the JSON fields object is an allow-list, so 0xFB-0xFD cannot be sent or seen through MeshChatX; title cannot be set.

Run: default inbound stamp cost is 8 (announced; sender solves ~4 s in pure Python, delivery 8.0 s); PATCH lxmf_inbound_stamp_cost 0 makes the announce carry nil and delivery 1.0 s. A reply to a peer that never announced returns 400 'Could not recall destination identity'; auto_announce is off by default.

Run: killing rnsd leaves MeshChatX serving HTTP ('Socket for LocalInterface was closed, attempting to reconnect'); after restart it reconnected in 7 s. A message sent during the outage was delivered once at +67.6 s (same hash, no loss) but the stale original kept emitting 'failed' 43 times and its stored row ended 'failed': state is not monotonic; disable auto_resend_failed_messages_when_announce_received and auto_send_failed_messages_to_propagation_node and treat delivered as sticky.

Run: hybrid works. rnsd 1.5.7 under system Python 3.10.12 (PYTHONPATH of the same hash-verified rns wheel plus cp310 cryptography) with MeshChatX on bundled CPython 3.11 as a shared-instance client delivered messages both ways, so L1's rnsd venv can stay on the distro Python.

Run: egress is zero. 10 minutes idle on both instances (02:17:02-02:27:12) and the whole ~25 minute session gave 0 packets to non-peer IPs (AF_PACKET logger on the veth; positive control with getent/curl showed DNS queries) and 0 non-AF_UNIX connect() calls across 6 strace logs. Probes of /community-interfaces, /update/check (enabled:false for pip installs) and /map/tiles (bundled mbtiles) also produced none. Static URLs (OSM tiles, nominatim, openfreemap, meshchatx.com directory, cdn.quad4.io updater, pypi.org) are browser-side or user-triggered.

Run: slim closure (35 wheels, no lxst/numpy/pycodec2/miniaudio/wasmtime/bleak/dbus-fast/aioquic/pylsqpack) is 33.2 MB of wheels, 128 MiB site-packages (23 MiB of it pip+setuptools), 74-75 MB RSS, 0.4 s warm start, and sent/received messages; those packages are imported lazily (src). It resolves as wheels on manylinux and musllinux for x86_64 and aarch64. Full closure: 251 MiB, 87.6 MB RSS, 1.6 s warm start (9.8 s first run).

MeshChatX README 'Project status': development and releases end 2027-01-01, v5.0.0 last release, repo archived afterwards (https://github.com/Quad4-Software/MeshChatX); no successor announced, 15 forks none above 1 star. Plain 'meshchatx --help' writes ~/.reticulum-meshchatx/logs/meshchatx.log (supervisor must set HOME); Landlock and seccomp self-sandboxing auto-enable on Linux.
result.recommendation: Fork: (A-full) MeshChatX full closure on a >=3.11 interpreter: supported but 251 MiB and an aarch64 miniaudio build. (A-slim) MeshChatX minus nine optional packages, bundled python-build-standalone 3.11 where distro python is older, rnsd left on the distro Python: 128 MiB, proven here for messaging, unsupported subset, sunset 2027-01-01. (B) liamcottle MeshChat 2.4.0: Python 3.10-compatible but no auth, no field 16, Node build. (C) sidecar importing RNS: fits every distro and Termux, gives verify flag and custom fields, needs the D17 #12 rule change. Pick: A-slim as the v1 carrier behind the carrier trait, hybrid with rnsd, with C ready; choose C now if the owner will not add an interpreter and wants Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 11 and Termux.
open_questions: Is a bundled CPython (python-build-standalone, MPL-2.0 repo, PSF interpreter, ~47 MB per arch) an acceptable new Layer 1 dependency, or should the floor rise to Debian 12+/Ubuntu 24.04+?

Is running MeshChatX with a deliberately reduced dependency set (no voice, WASM plugins, BLE RNode, WebTransport) acceptable, or must the full upstream closure ship (+120 MiB, aarch64 miniaudio source build)?
Adopt A-slim now and decide C when v5.0.0 lands (my default), or decide C now? Who owns a fork after 2027-01-01?
Announce policy and bridge display name (MeshChatX default 'Anonymous Peer', no auto-announce): who sets the interval given the LoRa 2 percent announce cap?
Must the Messages view show verified versus unverified LXMF senders (needs Option C), or is a blanket 'sender unverified' label enough for v1?
Does a Termux phone need its own LXMF carrier (compiling or CI-building Android wheels for cffi and cborx), or only the hub?
